look: A derelict, tin-roofed farm stand containing a cat bed but no produce opens onto a rutted dirt road, where dusk is closing in through thick fog.
Branches reach out over the road from both sides, far enough up that they almost meet in the middle.
Behind the stand a fence sags, four strands of wire on posts leaning crookedly.
Across the road the fog obscures something tall and unlit, too square to be trees.
Across the road the fog has thinned around a tall, unlit house.
Tire tracks show in the dried mud of the shoulder.
The air smells of cold and wet earth.
A tall foyer under a water-stained ceiling. The front door is shut behind you, with a crowded coat tree beside it and an empty cat bowl on the floor.
A cloudy mirror hangs by the door.
A stroller is parked in the corner by a pile of shoes and tiny booties.
A bulletin board hangs over a small table where a smart speaker blinks blue.
A shipping box sits half-opened against the wall.
An arched doorway opens on one side of the hall.
A wide doorway opens on the other.
The grand staircase is a ruin, with fresh lumber stacked beside it.
The grand staircase is mended most of the way up, but the top steps are still missing, with fresh lumber stacked beside its base.
A patched grand staircase sweeps up to the floor above.

Two dining chairs are pushed back from a long table, with a high chair beside. The tall windows above the sideboard look onto an overgrown garden. Through the arched doorway you can see a crowded coat tree, and a swinging door lets through the hum of a fridge.
A to-do list in pencil is propped against the lamp on the sideboard.

A big old-fashioned kitchen. A pasta pot sits on the cast-iron stove, a drying rack stands empty by the kitchen sink, and a Keurig waits with a clean mug. The fridge-freezer hums beside the trash can, a cake box sits at the end of the counter, and the pantry door is ajar. A swinging door shows a sliver of a long table each time it moves.
Through the glazed back door there are steps, then tangled green.

An overgrown sunken courtyard. Ivy swallows the side of the house, and a stone wall enclosed herb garden has run wild. A picnic blanket is spread over a stone bench. In the middle, a stone circle holds the last of a chalk diagram. An autumn-bronzed oak tree crowds the far wing of the house. Pumpkins wait by the kitchen steps next to a cat bowl, and at the top, the back door glows warm and smells faintly of coffee.

A room for long evenings: a deep sofa with a baby blanket, two armchairs, bookshelves and a fireplace full of cold ash. One armchair has been turned to face a bare patch of wall. A stack of board books sits on the rug. A tall curiosity cabinet stands in the corner. Through the wide doorway you can see the foot of a staircase and a pile of shoes.

A close little library with packed library shelves. A scorch circle is burned into the floorboards, with a spool of copper wire among the things scattered around it, and a spirit board lies just outside it. An empty cat bed sits in the corner. The air feels charged, like the moment before a storm. The back of a heavy cabinet fills one wall, a keyhole set at waist height, and behind the shelves a shaded library window stands open a crack.

A hallway lined with faded portraits, with a single door. A roll-top desk stands against the wall, and a heavy oak wardrobe looms beside it. The doorway seems to be to a bedroom. The staircase leads back down to the Entryway, its patched steps solid underfoot. Baby clothes hang over the railing to dry. A cat bowl sits at the top of the staircase. A bad smell hangs in the air.

A hallway lined with faded portraits, with two doors. A roll-top desk stands against the wall, and a heavy oak wardrobe looms beside it. One doorway seems to be to a bedroom, and a hum of white noise suggests the other doorway is a nursery. The staircase leads back down to the Entryway, its patched steps solid underfoot. Baby clothes hang over the railing to dry. A cat bowl sits at the top of the staircase. A bad smell hangs in the air.

A hallway lined with faded portraits, with two doors. A roll-top desk stands against the wall, and a heavy oak wardrobe looms beside it, a short crowbar lying on the floor against the skirting board. One doorway seems to be to a bedroom, and a hum of white noise suggests the other doorway is a nursery. The staircase leads back down to the Entryway, its patched steps solid underfoot. Baby clothes hang over the railing to dry. A cat bowl sits at the top of the staircase. A bad smell hangs in the air.

The main bedroom containing an unmade bed, a nightstand, and a dresser with a tall mirror by a sash window. In the corner sits an open moving box. The panelled bedroom door stands half open on the hallway.

A small, warm room painted a soft sage green. A mobile slowly turns above a crib, and a painted shelf runs along the wall above it. Faint, happy crackling noises come from the changing table. The nursery door, painted the same soft sage, is pushed to but not latched on the hallway.
